texts.orig: In this paper; a new Linear Consistency Test (LCT)-based attack against a noised pseudorandom generator scheme employing   irregular   clocking   is described and analyzed. The attack was applied specific representative of this class of generators known as The Binary Rate Multiplier (BRM). The  attack  first   assigns system of linear equations to the BRM based on guessed initial state of its clocking LFSR. This system is then checked for consistency and if consistent; the right initial state of the clocking LFSR was guessed. If the obtained system is inconsistent; the  equations involving complemented bits of the intercepted sequence are eliminated from the and then the consistency of the is checked Which bits  of the intercepted sequence are complemented is also   guessed. If the guess of   those bits is right,  the obtained will surely become consistent. Otherwise; if the guess of the initial state of the clocking LFSR was right, there is significant chance that the newly obtained system becomes consistent. In contrary case, the new system attack always gives the right solution for the initial state of the   clocking LFSR; but that solution may be accompanied by other solutions (false alarms). The recovery procedure in those cases is proposed as well. The attack is feasible if the number of possible combinations for the bits of the intercepted against system system again. system sequence complemented by noise is small, which means that the level of noise is up to moderate_
